raw_response:
I been farming these 8 mu for 40 years. Never went to school, but I know this land. Me and my old lady, just the two of us now. Last year I put 6 mu in corn and 2 mu in mungbean, worked out fine. This year I’ll do the same — no reason to change what you know.

For the corn: I plant around April 20th, when the dirt gets warm. I buy the hybrid seed from the shop in town, same kind my neighbors use. Costs me about 50 yuan per mu. Before planting, I spread half a big bag of that three-number compound fertilizer on each mu. Then when the corn grows to my knee, I topdress with one small bag of urea per mu. That’s what I did last year and got decent corn. I irrigate twice from the well — once after planting if the rain don’t come, and once when the tassels come out. Pumping water costs electricity, so I don’t water more than that. I spray herbicide once after planting, and if I see corn borers, I spray insecticide too. I’m hoping for around 450 kg per mu, same as last year if the weather holds. I hire my nephew’s tractor to plow in early April, and me and my wife do the rest.

For the mungbean: I plant the 2 mu near the house in late May, using seed I saved from last year — didn’t buy new. Mungbean is easy, don’t need much. I put down just a little compound fertilizer at planting, nothing like the corn. Water once if July is real dry. Spray herbicide once. Should get about 100 kg per mu, enough for us to eat and sell the rest.

Money is tight. Seed, fertilizer, pumping water, it all adds up. I’ll spend around 2,000 yuan on the corn alone, and not much on the mungbean. Me and my wife do most the work ourselves, but I’ll pay my nephew for a couple days to help plant the corn. That’s how we manage.
